examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_seed_hash(sketch) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) s;

name: datasketch_aod_similarity_test
description: Returns true if the Jaccard similarity of the key sets is at least the threshold, with high confidence (its lower bound is >= threshold)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_similarity_test(actual, expected, 0.9) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS actual FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS expected FROM range(100, 1100) t(i)) e;

name: datasketch_aod_summaries
description: Returns the retained entries of the array-of-doubles sketch as a list of {hash, values} structs (the key hash and its values)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_summaries(sketch) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) s;

name: datasketch_aod_to_theta
description: Converts the array-of-doubles sketch to a Theta sketch of its keys (dropping the summaries), usable with the datasketch_theta functions

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_to_theta(sketch) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) s;

name: datasketch_aod_union
description: Returns the union of two or more array-of-doubles sketches (values of a key summed element-wise) with the given log2 of nominal entries (lg_k, 4-26)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_union(16, sketch_a, sketch_b) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_a FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_b FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) b;

name: datasketch_aod_union
description: Returns the union of two or more array-of-doubles sketches (values of a key summed element-wise), keeping as many entries as the largest input (at least lg_k 12)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_union(sketch_a, sketch_b) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_a FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_b FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) b;

SELECT datasketch_aod_union(sketch_a, sketch_b, sketch_c) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_a FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_b FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) b, (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch_c FROM range(250, 1250) t(i)) c;

name: datasketch_aod_upper_bound
description: Returns the upper bound of the estimated number of distinct keys at the given number of standard deviations (1, 2, or 3)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_aod_upper_bound(sketch, 2) FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(i % 100, [1.0, i * 0.5]::DOUBLE[]) AS sketch FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) s;

name: datasketch_cpc_merge
description: Return the union of two CPC sketches as a new sketch. The result uses the smaller lg_k of the two inputs

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_cpc_merge(sketch_a, sketch_b) FROM (SELECT datasketch_cpc(12, i) AS sketch_a FROM range(100) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_cpc(12, i) AS sketch_b FROM range(50, 150) t(i)) b;

name: datasketch_hll_merge

name: datasketch_theta_blob
description: Hashes raw BLOB values (their bytes) into a Theta sketch, like datasketch_theta does for other types (datasketch_theta(BLOB) merges serialized sketches instead). Optional keyword arguments: seed (hash seed; sketches can only be combined with sketches built with the same seed) and p (sampling probability in (0, 1], to pre-sample the input)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_theta_blob(i::VARCHAR::BLOB) FROM range(1000) t(i);
SELECT datasketch_theta_blob(i::VARCHAR::BLOB, seed := 42) FROM range(1000) t(i);

name: datasketch_theta_dissimilarity_test
description: Returns true if the Jaccard similarity of the two sketches is at most the threshold, with high confidence (its upper bound is <= threshold)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_theta_dissimilarity_test(actual, expected, 0.1) FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS actual FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS expected FROM range(100, 1100) t(i)) e;

name: datasketch_theta_exactly_equal
description: Returns true if the two sketches retain exactly the same hashes with the same theta, i.e. they represent the same set as far as the sketches can tell

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_theta_exactly_equal(sketch_a, sketch_b) FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch_a FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch_b FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) b;

name: datasketch_theta_intersect_agg
description: Intersects Theta sketches across rows: the result estimates the number of distinct values present in every input sketch. NULL sketches are skipped; returns NULL if there are no sketches

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_theta_intersect_agg(sketch) FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch FROM range(0, 1000) t(i) UNION ALL SELECT datasketch_theta(i) FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) s;

name: datasketch_theta_jaccard
returnType: STRUCT(lower DOUBLE, estimate DOUBLE, upper DOUBLE)
description: Returns the Jaccard similarity |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B| of two sketches as a struct of its estimate and approximate lower and upper bounds (about 2 standard deviations). Two empty sketches are identical (1.0)

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_theta_jaccard(sketch_a, sketch_b) FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch_a FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch_b FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) b;

SELECT datasketch_theta_jaccard(sketch_a, sketch_b).estimate FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch_a FROM range(0, 1000) t(i)) a, (SELECT datasketch_theta(i) AS sketch_b FROM range(500, 1500) t(i)) b;

name: datasketch_tuple
description: Creates a Tuple sketch with the given log2 of nominal entries (lg_k, 4-26): a Theta sketch of the distinct keys where each retained key carries a DOUBLE summary of its values. Options: mode := 'sum' (default), 'min', 'max' or 'one' combines the values of a key; seed := (hash seed; sketches can only be combined with sketches built with the same seed); p := sampling probability in (0, 1]

examples.code: SELECT datasketch_tuple(14, user_id, amount) FROM (SELECT i % 100 AS user_id, i::DOUBLE AS amount FROM range(1000) t(i)) t;
SELECT datasketch_tuple(14, user_id, amount, mode := 'max', seed := 42) FROM (SELECT i % 100 AS user_id, i::DOUBLE AS amount FROM range(1000) t(i)) t;
